name: Crystal Lattice
description: Atomic pattern embodying harmony, resonance, and self-similarity across scales. Foundation for crystalline intelligence.

scope.definition: Fraction of ideal Bravais lattice sites occupied by the correct atom type in a high-quality silicon single crystal (defect density < 10¹⁰/cm³), measured by X-ray diffraction rocking curve.

evidence.source: Kittel (2004) 'Introduction to Solid State Physics', 8th ed., Wiley; Authier (2001) 'Dynamical Theory of X-ray Diffraction', Oxford UP.
cross_domain_examples: float-zone silicon: <5×10⁹ defects/cm³ — 0.9999999995 site occupancy — near-perfect crystal
diamond crystal: 0.998 lattice site occupancy with near-zero vacancy density at room temperature
NaCl ionic crystal: 0.995 ideal occupancy — Schottky defect density controlled by thermodynamics
protein crystal: 0.85-0.92 occupancy due to flexible loops and solvent inclusion

scope.falsifiability: If X-ray rocking curves show diffuse scattering exceeding 0.5% of Bragg peak intensity, defect density is too high for coherent lattice claim.
scope.measurement_limits: Occupancy approaches 1.0 only at temperatures near 0 K. Room temperature defect density is thermodynamically governed — Boltzmann distribution sets minimum defect concentration of ~10⁶/cm³.
